title: What If the World Ran Out of Sand?

scenes.text: What if the world ran out of sand? We use more of it than anything except water.
The UN says we dig up about fifty billion tonnes of sand and gravel a year. That's roughly triple the amount of two decades ago.
Most of it goes into concrete and glass, so cities, roads and windows all depend on it.
And it isn't renewable on our timescale. Nature takes hundreds of thousands of years to make it.
Digging it from rivers already hurts. In Vietnam's Mekong delta the land is sinking, and salt water ruins farmland.
In Sri Lanka, removing sand reversed a river's flow and sent seawater, and crocodiles, inland.
